belongs_to: Puzzle Time 'Square Pairs!': "Look at the following numbers: 3 6 10 15 1. They are arranged such that each pair of adjacent numbers adds up to a square. 3 + 6 = 9, 6 + 10 = 16, 10 + 15 = 25, 15 + 1 = 16."
description: A row of 5 numbers printed left to right in the running text line, separated by wide spaces, in this order: 3, 6, 10, 15, 1. They are plain printed digits: no boxes, no arrows, no colours, no brackets. Below the paragraph the four adjacent-pair sums are printed centred as text: 3 + 6 = 9, 6 + 10 = 16, 10 + 15 = 25, 15 + 1 = 16 (4 sums for the 4 adjacent pairs; 9, 16, 25, 16 are the squares).
unclear: The row of numbers is ordinary typeset text, not a drawn figure; it is listed because it is the one example arrangement the Puzzle Time works from. A reader may treat it as a number list / LaTeX line instead of a diagram.

belongs_to: Puzzle Time 'Square Pairs!': "Try arranging the numbers 1 to 17 (without repetition) in a row in a similar way - the sum of every adjacent pair of numbers should be a square. Can you arrange them in more than one way?" (the empty boxes to fill)
description: A single horizontal row of 17 EMPTY equal squares (verified by counting: 17), touching nothing, placed between the sentence 'Can you arrange them in more than one way? If not, can you explain why?' and the sentence 'Can you do the same with numbers from 1 to 32...'. Each square is pale yellow with a thin dark outline; all squares are the same size (about 24 px side on a 979 px wide page, i.e. a small square), evenly spaced with a gap about half a square wide (centre-to-centre pitch about 35 px), left end a little inside the left text margin and right end a little short of the right text margin. No numbers, no arrows, no labels, no colours other than the yellow fill. One box per number 1 to 17.

belongs_to: Puzzle Time 'Square Pairs!': "Can you do the same with numbers from 1 to 32 (again, without repetition), but this time arranging all the numbers in a circle?" (the ring of empty boxes to fill)
description: A ring (circle) of EMPTY equal squares drawn below the last sentence, centred on the page, about 400 px across on a 979 px wide page. Verified by counting and by measuring angles: 28 squares (not 32), evenly spaced about 12.9 degrees apart round the ring, one square exactly at the top (12 o'clock), one at the bottom (6 o'clock), one at the far left (9 o'clock) and one at the far right (3 o'clock), with 6 squares between each pair of neighbouring compass-point squares (4 x 7 = 28). Squares are all the same size (about 24 px side), upright (not rotated to follow the circle), pale pink/lilac fill with a thin dark outline; neighbouring squares are separated by a gap of about half a square or less, so the ring has no gaps and no overlaps. The ring is empty inside (the pale watermark text 'NCERT not to be republished' runs across the page, ignore it). No numbers, arrows or labels in or beside the squares. The cartoon children at the bottom of the page are decoration.
unclear: The text asks for the numbers 1 to 32 in a circle, but the printed ring has 28 boxes (counted twice: by eye on a zoomed crop and by detecting box outlines). Which count the plan should show is a decision for the map step (28 as printed, or 32 as the question needs).

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q8 (chapter p.10): "In the following pattern, fill in the missing numbers" - the printed answer (Ans.) on this page shows the completed pattern
description: The printed answer is a left-aligned block of 5 equations, one per line, right after 'Ans.': line 1: 1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2 = 3^2; line 2: 2^2 + 3^2 + 6^2 = 7^2; line 3: 3^2 + 4^2 + 12^2 = 13^2; line 4: 4^2 + 5^2 + 20^2 = (21)^2 (the 21 is bold and underlined, in brackets: the filled blank); line 5: 9^2 + 10^2 + (90)^2 = (91)^2 (the 90 and the 91 are each bold and underlined, in brackets: the two filled blanks). Pattern: a^2 + (a+1)^2 + (a(a+1))^2 = (a(a+1)+1)^2 with a = 1, 2, 3, 4 and 9 (third terms 2, 6, 12, 20, 90; right sides 3, 7, 13, 21, 91). So 3 blanks are filled in the answer: 21, 90 and 91. Lines 1 to 3 are complete as given in the question; line 4 had one blank (the square on the right) and line 5 had two blanks (the third term and the right side).
unclear: Typeset equations, not a drawn picture; listed because it is a number pattern with highlighted (underlined bold) filled-in answers. The question itself (the same five lines with blanks '(___)') is printed on chapter p.10-11 (pdf page 11), outside this page range.
